findings.title: Oracle Critical Security Patch Update Advisory - September 2026
findings.summary_md: Oracle's September Critical Security Patch Update lists CVE-2026-87268 in Oracle VM VirtualBox Core as a local, low-privilege flaw in version 7.2.16, with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 7.8 and confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact. The advisory credits James Forshaw for the report and says a successful attack can compromise Oracle VM VirtualBox. Its modification history records a 15 September 2026 initial release.

findings.title: Multiples vulnerabilites dans Oracle Virtualization (CERTFR-2026-AVI-1188)
findings.summary_md: CERT-FR published this advisory on 16 September 2026 covering multiple Oracle Virtualization flaws, including CVE-2026-87268, and names Oracle VM VirtualBox 7.2.16 as affected. It points administrators to Oracle's 15 September CSPU for fixes and lists risks that include arbitrary code execution, denial of service, and loss of confidentiality or integrity.

findings.title: CVE-2026-108398 Detail
findings.summary_md: NVD published CVE-2026-108398 on 13 October 2026, describing an untrusted search path in .NET Framework that lets an authorized attacker bypass a security feature locally. The record assigns a CVSS 3.1 base score of 8.8 with changed scope and links to Microsoft's update guide as its reference.

findings.title: October 2026 cumulative update - .NET Framework
findings.summary_md: Microsoft's October 2026 .NET Framework cumulative update, released 13 October, lists CVE-2026-108398 as a security feature bypass addressed in the release. Its product table maps the fix to per-OS KBs, including KB5127694 for Windows 11 26H2 with .NET Framework 3.5 and 4.8.1, and KB5127687 for Windows Server 2022 with .NET Framework 4.8.

findings.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What's a Single Bit Between Friends?
findings.summary_md: James Forshaw's 23 November Project Zero write-up details three new VirtualBox process-hardening bypasses and focuses on CVE-2026-87268, which abuses .NET Framework 4's fallback from image-mapped loading to FlatImageLayout when NtCreateSection returns STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT. He shows that clearing the IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE bit lets an untrusted assembly load under UMCI on Windows 11 S Mode and that COM hijacking of WerSecureFault.exe reaches PPL code execution. The post records an October fix for CVE-2026-108398 and notes the protected-process route remains unchanged.
